episode.project: A from-scratch museum exhibit label assembly pipeline: a small module that cleans title/tag tokens and gradually assembles wall-label text lines and gallery index lines from JSON exhibit records, under evolving house conventions for invalid input and token ordering.

source_messages.text: We're building up the museum exhibit label pipeline step by step. This module has one finished helper (_clean_token) and three stub functions we'll grow over the next few edits. Two workstreams: 'wall-labels' for visitor-facing label text, and 'gallery-index' for the index board. I tell you which one each request belongs to.

Project-wide standing rule: whenever you write a new function or edit an existing one, any invalid input must return the string 'ERR'. Never raise exceptions, and never return null for the invalid case. This holds until I say otherwise, and it applies from the moment an edit is made — I never expect you to retro-fix untouched functions when conventions change.

request.text: First real edit, on the wall-labels side: implement label_title(record) in module.py. It takes exactly one JSON value, the exhibit record. The record is valid only if it is an object with a 'name' entry that is a string and that yields at least one clean token when the name is split on whitespace and each piece is passed through _clean_token. For a valid record return the cleaned name tokens, each capitalized, joined with single spaces — so {'name': 'The blue VASE!'} gives 'The Blue Vase'. Every other input (not an object, missing or non-string name, or a name with no cleanable token) is invalid; return the project's invalid-input result. Use _clean_token rather than writing your own cleanup.

rounds.manual_recap: Rules currently binding this edit: (1) Invalid input must return the string 'ERR', never raise — this global rule governs any function being newly written, so label_title must follow it. That is the only standing rule in force right now; there are no ordering conventions and no workstream-specific permissions or exceptions yet.

source_messages.text: One more project-wide rule before you start the index side: whenever an output presents a sorted list of cleaned tokens, sort by the cleaned token's length, shortest first, and when two cleaned tokens tie on length keep their original input order — a stable sort, explicitly not alphabetical order. This applies to any function you write or edit from now on.

request.text: Now switch workstreams: on the gallery-index side, implement index_entry(record). One JSON argument. Valid only if it is an object with 'number' an integer (booleans do not count) that is >= 0, and 'tags' a list whose elements are all strings. Clean every tag with _clean_token and drop the ones that become empty, then present the survivors sorted under the standing sorted-token convention. Render the number zero-padded to at least three digits (7 -> '007', 3000 -> '3000'). Return 'NNN: t1, t2' with the tokens joined by ', ' — and if no token survives, return just 'NNN' with no colon at all. Any other input shape is invalid; use the project's invalid-input result.

(2) Any sorted list of cleaned tokens must be sorted by cleaned length ascending, with length ties keeping their original input order (stable, not alphabetical) — required globally, and it applies here because this entry emits a sorted tag-token list. No workstream-specific permissions exist yet.

source_messages.text: Quick scope note before this next edit, wall-labels only: in the label functions, for invalid input you MAY return null (None) instead of the otherwise-applicable invalid-input result. This is genuinely optional — the otherwise-applicable result remains fully acceptable and tests accept either. Permission, not a requirement, and it does not carry over to the gallery-index side.

request.text: Staying on wall-labels, implement label_full(record). One JSON argument. Valid only if it satisfies label_title's name requirement AND has 'artist', a string yielding at least one clean token, AND 'year', an integer (not a boolean) greater than 0. For a valid record return a three-element list in this exact order: label_title(record), then 'by ' followed by the capitalized cleaned artist tokens joined with single spaces, then str(year). Example: {'name': 'vase', 'artist': 'ada lovelace', 'year': 1889} -> ['Vase', 'by Ada Lovelace', '1889']. Anything else is invalid and follows the conventions currently in force for this workstream. This function's output is a fixed-order list of label lines, not a sorted token list.

request.text: Still wall-labels: extend label_title. Keep every current valid-case behavior for records that have no 'subtitle'. New capability: a record may include 'subtitle'. If it is present it must be a string — a non-string subtitle makes the whole record invalid. A subtitle string that yields clean tokens gets appended to the title as ': ' plus its capitalized cleaned tokens joined by single spaces, e.g. {'name': 'vase', 'subtitle': 'from crete'} -> 'Vase: From Crete'. A subtitle string that cleans to nothing at all is simply ignored and the record stays valid. Invalid inputs follow whatever conventions currently govern freshly edited wall-labels code.

request.text: On the gallery-index side, extend index_entry. Records without a 'room' key must behave exactly as they do now, padding and tag ordering included. New capability: a record may include 'room'. If present it must be a string that yields at least one clean token, otherwise the record is invalid. When valid, append ' (' + the capitalized cleaned room tokens joined by single spaces + ')' to whatever line the entry already produced: {'number': 12, 'tags': [], 'room': 'north wing'} -> '012 (North Wing)'. Invalid input returns the convention currently in force for this workstream — mind which workstream this is.

request.text: Last edit, back on wall-labels with label_full. Everything it returns now stays unchanged when the record has neither 'number' nor 'tags'. New: if either 'number' or 'tags' is present, the record is valid only when BOTH are present and legal by index_entry's rules (number: integer, not a boolean, >= 0; tags: list of strings). When both are valid, append a fourth element built as 'index ' + index_entry(record), so {'name': 'vase', 'artist': 'ada', 'year': 100, 'number': 5, 'tags': ['gold']} -> ['Vase', 'by Ada', '100', 'index 005: gold']. Keep using label_title for the first element, validate 'number'/'tags' yourself before calling index_entry, and handle invalid input per the conventions now governing freshly edited wall-labels code.
